weather.tip: 90% chance of rain today — carry an umbrella and build in extra commute time, especially on stretches prone to waterlogging like Agaram Road and the ORR service roads.

around.headline: Fake tax notices circulating on WhatsApp target ITR filers, malware steals banking credentials
around.summary: Scammers are sending fake income-tax notices over WhatsApp that, once opened, install malware capable of stealing banking credentials. Never open tax-notice links or attachments from WhatsApp — check your ITR status only via the official incometax.gov.in portal.

around.headline: Family friend stabs Bengaluru college student for bunking class to watch a movie
around.summary: A college student was stabbed by a family friend after being caught skipping class to watch a movie, underscoring how quickly a disagreement with someone close can turn violent. If a dispute with an acquaintance is escalating, remove yourself from the situation first and involve family or police rather than trying to de-escalate alone.

around.headline: Bengaluru Metro Phase 3 construction set to affect 1,087 properties along its corridor
around.summary: New reports indicate roughly 1,087 properties will be impacted by Phase 3 Metro construction as work ramps up across the corridor. If you live or work along a Phase 3 route, watch for official land-acquisition or construction notices in the coming weeks.

around.headline: BBMP to launch a fresh drive to enforce parking regulations across Bengaluru
around.summary: Civic authorities are preparing a new enforcement drive against illegal and haphazard parking in the city. Double-check where you park in commercial areas in the coming days, since fines and towing are likely to pick up once the drive begins.

around.headline: Cauvery protests intensify; Karnataka CM asks Tamil Nadu CM Vijay to defer his Bengaluru visit
around.summary: As protests over Karnataka's Cauvery water release to Tamil Nadu continue to grow, CM Siddaramaiah (DKS) has asked Tamil Nadu CM Vijay to put off a planned Bengaluru visit, on top of the statewide bandh already called for August 13. If you have travel, deliveries, or business plans around that date or involving a possible VIP visit, keep some flexibility in case of protests or shutdowns.

around.headline: Karnataka's toll revenue doubles to Rs 4,779 crore in 5 years as travel on the Bengaluru–Chennai expressway gets costlier
around.summary: State toll collections have doubled over five years amid surging highway traffic, and a fresh toll revision has made the Bengaluru–Chennai expressway more expensive to use. Budget a bit more for tolls if you're driving out of the city on this route soon.
around.source: The Times of India, Deccan Herald

around.headline: Iran-Israel-US tensions escalate; India voices concern over shipping and energy security
around.summary: Reports suggest the US and Israel are planning strikes on Iranian energy targets as soon as this weekend, and India's EAM S Jaishankar has conveyed concern to Iran's foreign minister about attacks on commercial shipping near the Gulf. A wider conflict could push global oil prices up, so expect possible pressure on fuel prices at home in the coming days.

street_smart.title: An auto driver hands you change for a large note, and one of the ₹500 notes feels slightly off — the print seems flatter than usual and you're not sure it has the usual security strip. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Real incident today: a man was booked in Bengaluru for trying to deposit fake Rs 500 notes, a reminder that suspect currency can turn up in ordinary change and that passing it on (even unknowingly) can land you in trouble (The Times of India).
street_smart.situation: You're still standing at the auto or shop counter, note in hand. This is the only moment you have real leverage — once you walk away, you can no longer prove who gave it to you.

choices.text: Check it right there in good light: tilt it to see if the security thread shifts colour from green to blue, feel for the raised (intaglio) print on Gandhi's portrait and the Ashoka Pillar, and hold it up to check the watermark. If it fails, politely refuse it and ask for a different note.
choices.feedback: Correct. Genuine notes have a handful of checkable features — the colour-shifting security thread, raised printing, and watermark are the fastest to verify without any special equipment — and checking before you leave is the only way to actually get a replacement note.

choices.text: Accept it anyway since the driver seems trustworthy, and figure you'll deal with it later if it turns out to be an issue.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. 'Deal with it later' usually means you're now stuck holding a note it's illegal to knowingly spend or deposit — as in today's Bengaluru case, attempting to pass on a suspect note is itself an offence, and by then you have no way to trace it back to who gave it to you.

choices.text: Refuse to accept any note that looks even slightly unusual and demand full cash back in different denominations, without actually checking it against any security feature.
choices.feedback: Refusing outright without checking risks rejecting a perfectly genuine note over normal wear, which just causes an avoidable argument. Check the specific features first — only refuse if it actually fails one.

choices.text: Accept it, and plan to quietly pass it along in a future transaction to someone else rather than deal with it yourself.
choices.feedback: Passing a note you suspect is fake to someone else just moves the legal risk onto them, and it's still an offence if you knew. The correct move if you're stuck with one is to hand it to a bank counter or the police, not spend it further.

takeaways: Check a suspect note before you leave the counter: tilt it for the green-to-blue colour-shifting security thread, feel for raised print on the portrait and Ashoka Pillar, and hold it to light for the watermark — walking away removes your only way to prove who gave it to you.

Never knowingly spend, deposit, or pass on a note you suspect is fake — doing so is itself an offence, as seen in today's Bengaluru case; instead, hand it in at a bank counter (which will impound it and give you a receipt) or to the police.
If a shop, driver, or vendor's change looks off, ask for a different note on the spot — it's a routine, low-conflict request, not an accusation.

quiz.question: Karnataka's Chief Minister has asked which state's Chief Minister to defer a planned Bengaluru visit amid growing Cauvery protests?
quiz.why: The Cauvery dispute is one of India's oldest interstate water conflicts, dating back over a century, and is now managed by the Cauvery Water Management Authority set up after a 2018 Supreme Court verdict.

quiz.question: According to a report today, what are fake tax notices circulating on WhatsApp actually designed to do?
options: Install malware that steals banking credentials
Redirect users to a fake government job portal
quiz.why: You can verify any real tax notice directly by logging into the official incometax.gov.in portal — genuine notices never require you to open a link or install anything from WhatsApp.

quiz.question: The Union Cabinet's newly approved 'Samudra Manthan' scheme, worth Rs 84,084 crore, is aimed at boosting which sector?
quiz.why: India imports a large share of its crude oil needs, so schemes that boost domestic oil & gas exploration are aimed partly at reducing that import dependence over time.

quiz.question: What is the minimum age required to contest election to the Rajya Sabha (Council of States)?
quiz.why: This is higher than the minimum age for the Lok Sabha (25 years), reflecting the Rajya Sabha's design as a more experienced, indirectly elected upper house.

quiz.question: Which gas makes up the largest share of Earth's atmosphere by volume?
quiz.why: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the atmosphere; oxygen, which we actually breathe to survive, is only around 21%.
